npm run build produces correct CJS + ESM output

summary: Updated vitest.config.ts coverage exclusions per S7. Removed Phase A exclusions for: src/create-menu.ts, src/raw-mode.ts, src/screen.ts, src/setup/**, src/menu/** (all now have test suites that provide meaningful coverage). Added new exclusions for: src/index.ts, src/types.ts (S7 explicit), src/setup/index.ts, src/menu/index.ts (re-export barrels with no logic). Retained src/raw-mode.ts and src/cli.ts exclusions — raw-mode requires a real TTY, cli.ts requires process.argv mocking; both are genuinely uncoverable in unit tests.
Coverage results: 98.25% statements, 93.1% branches, 100% functions, 98.43% lines — all well above the 80% thresholds. 13 test files, 224 tests, 0 failures.
npm run build: dual CJS+ESM output emits cleanly. CJS require('./dist/index.cjs') resolves createMenu as a function. TypeScript clean (tsc --noEmit).

comments.note: src/raw-mode.ts is excluded from coverage because all tests mock it out — the functions require a real TTY to execute. This is consistent with the plan's guidance: 'keep targeted exclusions for modules that cannot be meaningfully covered.' Similarly, src/cli.ts is excluded as it requires process.argv mocking. The six barrels/type-only files (index.ts, setup/index.ts, menu/index.ts, types.ts) are excluded as they contain no runtime logic.

summary: All 4 ACs verified. Build: CJS + ESM output emits cleanly (tsup dual build, DTS generated). CJS: require('./dist/index.cjs') resolves createMenu as function. Tests: 224/224 pass across 13 files. Coverage: 98.25% stmts / 93.1% branches / 100% functions / 98.43% lines — all well above 80% thresholds. S7 exclusions: interactive modules (src/setup/**, src/menu/**, src/screen.ts, src/create-menu.ts) now included in coverage and fully covered; src/index.ts + src/types.ts correctly excluded (barrels/type-only per S7); src/setup/index.ts + src/menu/index.ts excluded as re-export barrels with no logic (valid extension of S7 rationale); src/raw-mode.ts + src/cli.ts kept excluded — raw-mode functions are mocked via vi.spyOn in all tests and require process.stdin.setRawMode which is unavailable in non-TTY environments, consistent with 'keep exclusions for modules that cannot be meaningfully covered'.

comments.note: src/raw-mode.ts exclusion retention is justified: screen.test.ts mocks enterRawMode and restoreTerminal via vi.spyOn, so the actual TTY-dependent implementation is never exercised. The try/catch guards inside enterRawMode/exitRawMode/restoreTerminal call process.stdin.setRawMode which throws in non-TTY — consistent with the plan's 'keep targeted exclusions for modules that cannot be meaningfully covered' guidance.
No observations — code is clean and consistent.
